details.body: In crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs, `CRITICAL_MOLT_GH_RATIO` (line 12, value 0.3) is a file-level `const` that determines when molts unconditionally fail (GH < 30% of gh_min_d). The acceptance criteria require 'All molt-related thresholds and modifiers are named parameters in species/process data, not hardcoded constants.' Move this to a field on `ShrimpRuntimeParams` (e.g., `critical_molt_gh_ratio: f64` with default 0.3) and add a corresponding optional field in `ShrimpPreset`.

Current-schema save/load can advance newly added shrimp halfway through the molt cycle. AnimalState still defaults inter_molt_timer_days to 14.0 (crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:615), AddShrimp seeds the adult stage timer to 0 without syncing that legacy field (crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:818-823), and normalize_loaded_shrimp_reproduction_state() blindly backfills any all-zero stage timers from inter_molt_timer_days (crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:946-960). A fresh v13 save with newly added adults will therefore reload with adult.molt_timer_days = 14.0 instead of 0. Restrict that backfill to migrated pre-v13 payloads, or only run it when the stage timer fields were absent in the source JSON.

Cold-water molt failures are misreported. molt_cycle() multiplies success by temp_condition_factor() for both below- and above-optimal temperatures (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:440-441, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:504-506), but emit_molt_failure() and emit_molt_stress_warning() only add a temperature cause when temperature_c > optimal_temp_max_c (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1113-1118, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1161-1163). In a cold tank, the new mechanic can fail molts while emitting only PoorCondition, which hides the actual driver. Add an explicit low-temperature cause/detail, or at minimum include any non-optimal temperature penalty in the event summary.

Reserve depletion is part of the new success formula, but it is not surfaced in failure diagnostics. The success path feeds reserve_g into molt_condition_modifier() (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:502-503, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1258-1276), yet emit_molt_failure() only reports a raw condition index when it blames PoorCondition (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1120-1127). A reserve-driven failure can therefore log a seemingly healthy condition value with no reserve/starvation hint. Include reserve-per-shrimp or reserve shortfall in the event details, or emit a starvation/reserve cause code when that branch drives the failure.

The ‘very low GH forces failure’ cutoff is still a hidden magic threshold. CRITICAL_MOLT_GH_RATIO is hardcoded at 0.3 (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:12) and applied directly in the failure gate (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:439, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:508) instead of coming from ShrimpRuntimeParams. That leaves one of the new molt-failure boundaries untunable and without preset/provenance coverage. Promote this cutoff into named runtime/preset data, or derive it from the existing named GH parameters rather than keeping a hidden constant.

Fix failing test `test_salt_treatment_emergency_scenario` in `crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs`. The `salt_treatment_source_profile()` helper constructs a `SourceWaterProfile` by copying DIC and alkalinity concentrations from the tank state, but the resulting DIC/alkalinity combination produces a pH that fails `validate_source_water_carbonate_profile()` with `InvalidSourceProfile { field: "carbonate_derived_ph", value: 8.5 }`. The source profile needs its DIC and alkalinity values adjusted (or a valid carbonate equilibrium explicitly set) so the profile passes validation when inserted into the source water catalog.

In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs`, the `molt_cycle` function also has a legacy-timer fallback (lines 508-523) that duplicates the migration logic in `save.rs:normalize_loaded_shrimp_reproduction_state`. With the new schema version guard in save.rs (only applying the fallback for `source_schema_version < PER_STAGE_MOLT_TIMER_SCHEMA_VERSION`), the runtime fallback in `molt_cycle` remains unconditional and will silently override zero stage timers from `inter_molt_timer_days` even on schema-14 saves. Consider whether the runtime fallback should also be guarded or removed, since its presence means the migration fix in save.rs is partially dead code for the runtime path.

Fix [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-151]: the rewritten emergency scenario no longer proves that chloride protection is what lowered mortality. The helper at [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-88] builds replacement water from `WaterState::default_for_volume_l(1.0)` ([crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:87-109]), so the 50% water change also reduces TAN/DOC/DON and changes alkalinity, DIC, and DO, while the assertion at [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:109-151] compares pre-treatment vs post-treatment mortality inside the same evolving run instead of against a matched control. In a local probe, that assertion still held with `chloride_protection_factor = 0.0`, so this test can pass even if chloride protection itself is broken. Use a parallel untreated/control tank, or a second water-change control that keeps every field identical except chloride/sodium, so the test actually guards the chloride-specific mechanic.

In `molt_condition_breakdown` (shrimp.rs:1419), the reserve target fraction `0.1` is hardcoded: `let reserve_target_g = wet_biomass_g * LIVE_BIOMASS_ORGANIC_FRACTION_G_PER_G * 0.1;`. This constant defines the minimum reserve-per-shrimp for a healthy molt. The acceptance criteria state 'all molt-related thresholds and modifiers are named parameters in species/process data, not hardcoded constants.' Promote this to a named field on `ShrimpRuntimeParams` (e.g., `molt_reserve_fraction`) with a default of 0.1, and expose it in the species TOML.

In `molt_condition_breakdown` (shrimp.rs:1427), the condition-vs-reserve weights `0.75` and `0.25` are hardcoded: `(0.75 * condition_index.clamp(0.0, 1.0) + 0.25 * reserve_factor)`. Similarly, the `reserve_factor` lower bound of `0.4` (line 1421) is hardcoded. These directly shape molt success probability. Consider promoting at least the condition/reserve split weights to named parameters so the relative importance of body condition vs. energy reserves can be tuned without code changes.

In `molt_cycle` (shrimp.rs:653-659), `failed_molt_accum * 0.5` is added to `molt_stress_index` after `update_molt_stress()` has already set a baseline. In `compute_mortality_probabilities` (shrimp.rs:1048+1052), `molt_stress_index` enters `stress_total` via `(molt_stress_index - 0.5).max(0.0)` AND `failed_molt_accum` enters independently via `molt_mortality = failed_molt_accum * failed_molt_mortality_scale`. This means `failed_molt_accum` drives mortality through two additive channels simultaneously. Add an inline comment at both sites documenting this intentional double-contribution so future maintainers don't 'fix' one path thinking the other is sufficient.

In `molt_cycle` (shrimp.rs:515-516), `temp_condition_factor(state.water.temperature_c, &params)` is called twice — once as `temp_factor` with `.max(0.25)` floor (for interval division safety) and once as `thermal_factor` (raw, for success score). Compute the raw value once, then derive both: `let raw_temp = temp_condition_factor(...); let temp_factor = raw_temp.max(0.25); let thermal_factor = raw_temp;`.

Fix `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:575-624`: `molt_cycle()` checks `readiness = timer_days / effective_interval` before incrementing `molt_timer_days`, then increments the timer after the resolution branch. A cohort that starts at `0.0` therefore resolves on daily step `interval + 1` instead of on the configured interval (for example, a 28-day adult interval resolves on day 29, and a 14-day juvenile interval resolves on day 15). That makes the species cadence parameters systematically one day slower than the values in data. Either increment the timers before the readiness check or compute readiness from the post-step timer.

Fix the mismatch between the modeled high-GH penalty and the failure diagnostics. `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1389-1400` reduces `molt_mineral_modifier()` when `gh_d > gh_max_d`, which can push a healthy shrimp below `molt_success_threshold`. But `emit_molt_failure()` at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1180-1232` only reports low GH/Ca/Mg and otherwise falls back to `PoorCondition`, so a very hard-water failure can be logged as `condition 1.00` even though the modeled driver was excessive GH. Either surface a high-GH/high-mineral diagnostic or remove the above-range GH penalty from the molt mechanic.

Re-tighten `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:1095-1118`. This test explicitly disables shrimp mortality at `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_baseline_scenarios.rs:1048-1049`, but the updated day-60/day-90 envelopes now accept `shrimp_count(0, ...)`, `juveniles_count(0, ...)`, and zero reproductive readiness. That means a total colony collapse after an early hatch pulse would still satisfy the checkpoint envelopes, materially weakening the regression that is supposed to guard the controlled ideal reproduction path. Restore non-zero floors at those checkpoints.

The new alkalinity budget overloads a public mg-based API with meq values. `BudgetDelta::alkalinity` is stored in `ElementBudget { in_mg, out_mg }` ([crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:34], [crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:68]), and `SystemElementDelta` exposes the same `*_mg` fields for `Element::Alkalinity` ([crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:64], [crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:78]). The mismatch is already observable in the helper output: `assert_budget_balanced` and `assert_per_tick_balanced` still print `mg` for alkalinity entries ([crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:472], [crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:494]). This silently breaks the meaning of the serialized/debug budget surface and makes alkalinity diagnostics unreliable for downstream consumers.

The `egg_drop_temp_swing_c` parameter (defined in `biology.rs:350`, defaulted in `biology.rs:850`, serialized in `neocaridina_davidi.toml`, and tested for `> 0.0` in `reproduction_factors.rs:542`) is never actually used in any logic. The `egg_dropping()` function only reads `egg_drop_instability_threshold` and the instability index. Either remove the unused parameter or wire it into the egg-dropping logic as the comment on `shrimp.rs:743` implies it should be ("A temperature swing > `egg_drop_temp_swing_c` in 24 hours...").

`EventCause::HighDensity` (defined at `events.rs:49`) is added by this changeset but never emitted anywhere. If density-dependent reproduction suppression is intended to be observable through events, wire it up (e.g., in spawning or reproductive readiness). Otherwise remove it to avoid dead code.

[high] `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:741-761` regresses sudden egg-drop behavior. The new code no longer reads `egg_drop_temp_swing_c` and only gates on `instability_index`, but `update_stability_tracker()` only moves that index 30% toward the raw swing each day (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:194-205`). From a stable baseline, even a 4°C swing produces only ~0.3 instability, which is still below the default `egg_drop_instability_threshold` of 0.5, so first-day temperature shocks no longer drop eggs at all. That also leaves the species parameter declared at `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:347-353` effectively dead.

[high] `crates/tank_core/tests/reproduction_factors.rs:227-245` breaks `test_reproduction_increases_with_condition`. The 'starved' setup zeroes `shrimp_periphyton_grazing_g_per_shrimp_per_day`, and `update_condition()` treats zero food demand as fully satiated (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:393-399`). In practice the starved tank ends up healthier than the fed tank, and `cargo test -p tank_core --test reproduction_factors` now fails at `crates/tank_core/tests/reproduction_factors.rs:252-265`.

[high] `crates/tank_core/tests/reproduction_factors.rs:560-599` still leaves `test_mature_stable_tank_breeds_well` failing. With the retuned scenario (`adult.count = 20`, `Feed { grams: 0.2 }`, faster maturation, etc.), the run only produces one `ShrimpBerried` event, so the `berried_events >= 3` assertion at `crates/tank_core/tests/reproduction_factors.rs:597-600` trips under `cargo test -p tank_core --test reproduction_factors`.

In `molt_cycle` (shrimp.rs lines 649-654), the `failed_molt_accum` increment rate (0.3 per failed stage) and decrement rate (0.35 per successful stage) are hardcoded constants, not named parameters. Per the acceptance criteria, 'All molt-related thresholds and modifiers ... are named parameters in species/process data, not hardcoded constants.' These constants directly govern the dynamics of molt failure accumulation and should be promoted to named fields on `ShrimpRuntimeParams` and set in `neocaridina_davidi.toml`.

The integration test `test_soft_vs_hard_water_shrimp_survival` uses the `ro_like` source water profile, which has `calcium_mg_per_l = 20.0` and `magnesium_mg_per_l = 5.0` — exactly matching the species minimums (`ca_min_mg_per_l = 20.0`, `mg_min_mg_per_l = 5.0`). This means the Ca and Mg factors in `molt_mineral_modifier` are both 1.0 (no penalty). The soft-water case only tests the GH penalty (~4.0 dGH < 5.0 dGH min), not individual Ca/Mg deficiency. The acceptance criteria says 'both calcium and magnesium contribute to the mineral modifier' should be verified in integration, but only the unit test covers this. Either lower the ro_like Ca/Mg values below the species minimums (e.g., Ca=10, Mg=2) or use a custom profile in the integration test that exercises all three mineral channels.

In `emit_molt_failure` (shrimp.rs lines 1362-1368), when no specific diagnostic threshold is triggered (GH is marginally low but above the event threshold, condition is above 0.65, reserves are adequate, etc.), the function defaults to `EventCause::PoorCondition` even though poor condition may not be the actual cause. A marginal miss on the combined `success_score` (e.g., 0.54 vs 0.55 threshold) from multiple slightly-below-optimal factors produces a misleading cause code. Consider adding a `MarginalFailure` or generic cause, or including the computed `success_score` and threshold in the event summary so the player can see the actual gap.

In `emit_molt_failure`, several diagnostic thresholds are hardcoded: the instability trigger at 0.3 (line 1337) and the poor-condition trigger at 0.65 (line 622 in `molt_cycle`). These thresholds determine which cause codes appear on MoltFailure events. While less critical than the core molt formula parameters, they affect player-visible diagnostics and should at minimum be documented constants or, ideally, configurable.

The `failed_molt_accum` feeds into mortality through two independent channels: (1) directly via `molt_mortality = failed_molt_accum * failed_molt_mortality_scale` in `compute_mortality_probabilities` (line 1184), and (2) indirectly via `molt_stress_index += failed_molt_accum * 0.5` (line 677) which then contributes via `(molt_stress_index - 0.5).max(0.0)` in the stress_total (line 1178). The code comments acknowledge this as intentional, but the 0.5 blending factor on line 677 is hardcoded and not a named parameter. At `failed_molt_accum = 1.0`, the combined daily mortality contribution can reach ~0.25 (0.15 direct + ~0.10 indirect), which means near-total population wipeout within a week. This aggressive coupling should be documented more clearly and the 0.5 blending factor should be a named parameter.

crates/tank_core/tests/reproduction_factors.rs:888-932 only records `max_tan`, `max_no2`, and `max_instability` from one snapshot per `run_day()` call, after 24 simulated hours have already elapsed. That means the new 'stable tank keeps chemistry in range' assertions cannot see any intra-day TAN/NO2/instability spikes between the feed at hour 0 and the day-end snapshot. A regression that creates dangerous hourly excursions but settles by the end of the day would still pass this test.

crates/tank_core/tests/reproduction_factors.rs:243-289 no longer isolates instability as the reason readiness stays low after a swing. The test now drives the tank to 36 C and then checks for 2-3 days of reduced readiness, but that same pattern can be produced by the direct temperature penalty and the condition/molt damage from the hot day even if post-swing readiness stops consulting `stability_tracker.instability_index`. The test verifies that instability remains elevated, but it does not prove that lingering instability is what is suppressing readiness.

Hardcoded 0.6 threshold in `emit_molt_stress_warning` (shrimp.rs:1411) should be a named parameter in ShrimpRuntimeParams. The acceptance criteria explicitly require 'All molt-related thresholds and modifiers are named parameters in species/process data, not hardcoded constants.' This threshold controls when the MoltStressWarning event fires and is not tunable.

Hardcoded magic numbers in `update_molt_stress` (shrimp.rs:480,493-497,502,504): the blend weights (0.5/0.3/0.2 for mineral stress components, 0.3/0.3/0.2/0.2/0.3 for stress pressure), and smoothing constants (rise=0.2, decay=0.05) are all hardcoded. These directly shape how mineral deficits translate into molt stress, which is a primary channel of the molt mechanics. Extract at least the rise/decay rates and the mineral-stress component weights into named parameters.

Hardcoded 0.5 threshold in `compute_mortality_probabilities` (shrimp.rs:1196): `(state.animal.molt_stress_index - 0.5).max(0.0)` uses a hardcoded activation threshold for when molt stress begins contributing to the general stress_total that drives mortality. This should be a named parameter.

Hardcoded `10.0` divisor in GH-excess penalty (shrimp.rs:1679) and hardcoded `0.3` floor clamp for Ca/Mg factors (shrimp.rs:1684,1689) in `molt_mineral_modifier`. These control the penalty curve shape for high-GH scenarios and the minimum contribution from individual minerals. Extract as named parameters (e.g., `gh_excess_penalty_divisor`, `mineral_factor_floor`).

Avoid running the same habitat probes twice under identical seeds/artifact labels. `all_habitat_geometry_probes_summary` re-invokes every probe in `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_habitat_geometry_probes.rs:1342-1405`, even though those same probes are still standalone `#[test]`s at `:249`, `:521`, `:712`, `:900`, and `:1185`. `HarnessRun::artifact_dir` is derived only from `scenario_id`, `artifact_label`, and seed in `crates/tank_harness/src/lib.rs:624-640`, so under Rust's default parallel test execution the summary test and the corresponding individual test can race on the same temp directory and clobber failure artifacts.

Tighten the light-depth probe so it actually requires plant growth, not just 'less negative growth'. The only semantic check is `growth_shallow > growth_deep` in `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_habitat_geometry_probes.rs:627-657`. On the current test run that passes with both values negative (`shallow=-0.4029 g`, `deep=-0.7110 g`), so the probe reports success even though neither tank experienced the documented 'more plant biomass growth after 14 days'.

Remove the built-in nitrifier advantage from the biofilter-scaling setup. In `crates/tank_harness/tests/e2e_habitat_geometry_probes.rs:310-317`, each run seeds nitrifier biomass as `carrying_capacity * INITIAL_CAPACITY_FRACTION`, and `carrying_capacity` itself depends on filter-media area. Because the larger-media run is constructed with the same seed path at `:322-335`, it starts with more nitrifier biomass before any simulation dynamics occur, then the assertions at `:435-457` check for lower reduced-N exposure and higher final nitrifier biomass. That makes the probe partially tautological and weakens its ability to catch regressions in the actual biofilter growth/capacity behavior.

The `molt_stress_pressure_*_weight` defaults sum to 1.3 (mineral 0.3 + instability 0.3 + condition 0.2 + thermal 0.2 + hourly 0.3) rather than 1.0. The mineral sub-weights (gh/ca/mg) DO have a `check_sum_close_to_one` invariant, and the condition/reserve blend weights also have one, but the pressure blend has no such check. The result is clamped to [0,1] so no numeric out-of-range occurs, but the oversubscribed sum means multiple moderate stressors saturate the clamp more easily than a unit-normalized blend would. If this is intentional (sensitivity coefficients rather than a probability partition), add a comment explaining the design choice in `update_molt_stress`. If not intentional, either normalize the defaults to sum to 1.0 or add a `check_sum_close_to_one` invariant for transparency. Files: crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs (lines 997-1015 default fns), crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs (lines 498-503 blend), crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs (missing sum check around line 499).

Add `failed_molt_accum` and `molt_readiness` to the tracing system (crates/tank_core/src/tracing.rs around line 326-366) alongside the existing `animal.molt_stress` trace point. These two state variables drive mortality independently of daily events and are key to diagnosing multi-day failure cascades, but are currently invisible in traces and snapshots. The acceptance criteria require 'Events, tracing, or snapshots expose enough detail to explain why molt failure occurred' — events cover single-day diagnostics well, but `failed_molt_accum` accumulates across days and its trajectory is not observable.

Keep the new alkalinity constant synchronized across the runtime and preset defaults. ProcessParams::default() now uses NITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N (crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:337-338), but the shipped process preset still hardcodes 0.1428 in crates/tank_data/data/process/default.toml:52-54 and crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1015-1019, and scenario construction copies the preset value into ProcessParams (crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:346-392). That leaves two different 'default' initialization paths with slightly different chemistry behavior.

The default values for `tan_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l` (2.0) and `no2_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l` (1.0) produce effective suppression spans of 1.0 and 0.5 respectively, whereas the old formulas used `threshold * 2.0` giving spans of 2.0 and 1.0. This makes TAN/NO2 reproduction suppression 2x more aggressive than the prior behavior. This causes `controlled_ideal_reproduction_path_still_hatches` to fail (readiness 0.339, expected [0.35, 0.85]). Either adjust the defaults to preserve the old curve shape (TAN full-suppression = 3.0, NO2 full-suppression = 1.5), or update the test envelope bounds to accommodate the intentionally steeper suppression. The choice should be explicit and documented.

`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:324-327` defines `molt_failure_poor_condition_threshold` as a threshold on the blended molt-condition score, but `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:623-638` records `poor_condition_involved` from that blended `condition_factor` while `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1396-1401` reports the failure as `condition {raw_condition}<{threshold}` using `min_condition_index`. That can produce impossible diagnostics for reserve-driven failures: a shrimp with healthy raw condition but low reserves can trip `PoorCondition` and emit text like `condition 0.70<0.65`. Either gate `PoorCondition` on raw `condition_index`, or keep the blended-factor test and report the blended factor/reserve shortfall instead of the raw condition index.

In `molt_mineral_modifier()` (shrimp.rs:1732-1734), the GH deficit penalty uses a quadratic formula `(gh_ratio)²` with NO floor clamp on the intermediate result, while `gh_mineral_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1677) uses a linear formula `gh_ratio` WITH a floor clamp to `mineral_factor_floor`. The docstring on `molt_mineral_factor_floor` (biology.rs:382-386) says the floor applies to 'GH/Ca/Mg factors inside `molt_mineral_modifier` and the shared reproduction GH penalty curve', but the GH factor in `molt_mineral_modifier` is computed as `gh_ratio * gh_ratio` and never clamped to the floor before multiplication. At GH=0.5 dGH (gh_min_d=5.0), the quadratic result is 0.01, well below the documented floor of 0.3. Either apply `.max(mineral_factor_floor)` to `gh_factor` in the deficit branch of `molt_mineral_modifier` (line 1734), or update the docstring to clarify that the floor only applies to Ca/Mg sub-factors and the reproduction curve, not the molt GH factor.

Hardcoded thermal divisors in `temp_condition_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1595 and 1597): the constants 10.0 (cold divisor) and 8.0 (hot divisor) control how quickly molt success degrades at non-optimal temperatures but are not exposed as named parameters in `ShrimpRuntimeParams`. The same 8.0 divisor appears hardcoded in `update_molt_stress()` (shrimp.rs:492). Extract these into named parameters (e.g., `temp_condition_low_divisor_c`, `temp_condition_high_divisor_c`) in `ShrimpRuntimeParams` with serde defaults, so they are inspectable and tunable through species data files as required by the acceptance criteria.

The condition stress midpoint in `update_molt_stress()` (shrimp.rs:490) is hardcoded as `0.5`: `let condition_stress = (0.5 - state.animal.population_condition_index()).max(0.0)`. This threshold controls when poor condition starts contributing to the molt stress index but cannot be tuned through species data. Similarly, the thermal stress clamp max of 0.5 on line 492 is hardcoded. Both should be named parameters.

The NH3 stress threshold (0.02 mg/L) and response scale (2.0) in `step_hourly_shrimp_stress()` (shrimp.rs:123-124) are hardcoded: `if nh3_mg_l > 0.02 { state.animal.hourly_nh3_stress_accum += (nh3_mg_l - 0.02) * 2.0 / 24.0; }`. These feed into the stress_total that drives mortality, including molt-stress-linked mortality. Extract them as named parameters.

The integration test `test_soft_vs_hard_water_shrimp_survival` (molt_mineral_budget.rs:726-748) asserts only that `hard_population - soft_population >= 5` over 1000 simulated hours starting from 36 shrimp. This is an extremely weak assertion — a gap of 5 is ~14% mortality difference, while the mineral modifier for the soft profile (Ca=10, Mg=2) should produce a modifier around 0.12, causing near-certain molt failures. The test should assert a more meaningful population gap (e.g., >= 15) or assert that the soft-water population drops below a specific threshold (e.g., < 20). The adjacent seeds (9000 vs 9001) also introduce unnecessary RNG variance; consider using the same seed to isolate the mineral effect.

The test `test_very_low_gh_causes_molt_deaths` (molt_mineral_budget.rs:282-286) asserts `final_count < 30` starting from 30 shrimp over 500 hours with Ca=1.5 mg/L, Mg=0.3 mg/L. A single death satisfies this assertion. Tighten to something like `final_count < 25` or assert a minimum number of MoltFailure events that led to deaths.

In `molt_mineral_modifier()` (shrimp.rs:1734), the GH deficit path uses a quadratic penalty `gh_ratio * gh_ratio` while Ca and Mg use linear ratios with sqrt deemphasis (lines 1742, 1747). This creates a ~3x sensitivity imbalance: at 50% of minimum, GH factor = 0.25 while Ca factor = sqrt(0.5) = 0.707. The design intent may be correct (GH is the aggregate measure), but verify this is intentional by adding a code comment explaining why different exponents are used for GH vs individual minerals.

In `shrimp.rs` line 554, the `critical_gh_deficit` check `(gh_d / params.gh_min_d.max(0.01)) < params.critical_molt_gh_ratio` does not guard against `gh_min_d = 0.0` the same way `molt_mineral_modifier` does. When a user sets `gh_min_d = 0.0` (semantically 'no GH minimum'), the `.max(0.01)` guard converts it to 0.01, causing any GH below `0.01 * critical_molt_gh_ratio = 0.003` to falsely trigger a critical deficit override. The fix is to add a check: `let critical_gh_deficit = params.gh_min_d > 0.0 && (gh_d / params.gh_min_d.max(0.01)) < params.critical_molt_gh_ratio;`. The existing test `test_zero_ca_and_mg_min_parameters_use_defensive_guards` (line 411) does not check `last_molt_success` and misses this edge case — it should assert that molt succeeds when all minimums are disabled.
